statement: The system shall support moving large ARC collections into WARC with confidence.
The system shall process collections at scale without becoming too manual or fragile.
The suite shall let staff quickly inspect the produced output.
Different institutions shall be able to deploy and test the tools in a reasonably consistent way.
The system shall detect duplicates.
The system shall produce useful reports for decision-making.
The system shall support archivists and technical staff as the main day-to-day users who run migrations, check records, and troubleshoot issues.
The system shall support managers and project leads who need information about progress, risks, and whether a batch is ready to move forward.
The system shall support preservation or QA staff who need evidence that the output is trustworthy.
The system shall provide detailed, machine-readable results in formats such as CSV or JSON for operators.
The system shall provide human-readable logs that operators can scan for errors.
The system shall provide summaries, counts, exception reports, and dashboards or concise PDF-style reports for decision-makers.

The system should ideally identify obvious repeats across related collections.

Processing shall be steady and predictable enough to run overnight or over a weekend for larger jobs.

The same workflow shall work for both smaller institutions and high-volume sites.
In most cases, the system shall process records as a stream or in small chunks so large migrations remain stable.
The system shall retain intermediates when the user has explicitly asked to keep them for debugging.
If chunking is not possible, the system shall make that very clear and fail safely rather than quietly consuming too much memory.
